newsitem.title: UK: Soybeans rally on U.S. crop data, Brazil weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: Soybeans rally on U.S. crop data, Brazil weather concerns.

text.p: Chicago soybean prices advanced on Monday in fast trading in a market buoyed by Friday's bullish U.S. crop and stocks reports.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Friday pegged 1996 U.S. soybean production and stocks at levels below expectations. Production was set at 2.38 billion bushels.
Support for prices also came from some concern about reports of hot weather in parts of Brazil's soybean growing region.

January soybean futures on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) touched an intra-day high at $7.34-1/2 per bushel, which was up almost nine cents on the day and followed gains of almost 30 cents on Friday. But wheat futures remained below the $4 per bushel barrier despite Friday's data that reported the lowest American winter wheat plantings since 1978.
Gold closed in London at $359.05 per ounce, little changed from Friday and holding above recent 3-1/4 year lows below $354.

The Dutch central bank announced it had sold 300 tonnes of gold from reserves recently. Earlier rumours of a central bank sale had depressed bullion. The confirmation was greeted with some relief by dealers.
Oil prices were little changed. London copper and aluminium extended recent gains on tight nearby stocks and technical signals, but coffee eased on trade selling after a rally stalled.
